extension.name: GitHub Project Lifecycle Sync
extension.description: Mirror each Spec Kit feature onto a GitHub Project (v2): create a parent feature issue, advance its Status column through the Spec Kit lifecycle (open -> analysis -> engineer-review -> ready -> in-progress -> in-review -> done), and, in standalone use, create one native sub-issue per task and close it as its task is checked off (under Sanduq Workflow, Workflow owns task issues). Board-agnostic initialization lets each repo choose required/automatic or optional/manual sync hooks. Idempotent and no-regress.
extension.author: Samy K. Abushanab

pageProps.readmeContent: # Project sync (`project`) **Purpose:** mirror each Spec Kit feature on a GitHub Project (v2). Project creates a parent issue, moves its Status column through the lifecycle and, in standalone use, creates one sub-issue per task. | | | | --- | --- | | Lifecycle phase | After `specify`, `plan`, `analyze` and `tasks`; before and after `implement` | | Hooks | Six optional hooks; Project Init can make them mandatory ([hooks](../reference/hooks.md)) | | Commands | `init`, `sync` ([reference](../reference/commands.md#project)) | | Requires | Python 3.11 or later; uses `gh` when available | | Standalone | Yes | | License | MIT | ## Setup ```bash specify extension add project gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project,read:project ``` ```text /speckit-project-init Discover the booking application's Project, map lifecycle columns, and select required sync. ``` Init asks whether sync hooks are **required** (automatic) or **optional** (ask first). It maps each phase to a real board column and writes `config.json`. Commit it with `.specify/extensions.yml`. ## Example ```text /speckit-project-sync Synchronize the refund parent and completed task IDs without duplicate sub-issues. ``` For a dry run, call the sync script directly: `python .specify/extensions/project/scripts/project_sync.py --phase auto --dry-run`. Add `--summary` for one result line (`ok`, `skipped` or `error`). ## How it runs ![Project sequence: project.init discovers and approves the board mapping and sync policy (required, optional or manual); when a Spec Kit phase completes, project.sync reconciles the actual board columns and records the result, and a skipped sync does not count as complete.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samykabu/sanduq/main/docs/diagrams/extension-project.animated.svg) Required sync runs automatically at each phase. Optional hooks ask first. In the managed Workflow, Workflow requires automatic sync and its own adapter creates and closes task sub-issues. Each Workflow claim names the phase and the exact sync command, so the dispatcher runs it without opening the sync command file. Workflow's board mode (`init --board full|minimal|none`) decides which phases it writes: `minimal` writes only Ready, In progress, In review and Done without task sub-issues, and `none` runs without a board. [Editable source](../diagrams/extension-project.html). ## Limits - If `gh`, its scopes, a GitHub remote or `config.json` is missing, sync logs a skip and exits 0. A skip is not a completed sync. - A malformed `.specify/project-sync-state.json` stops the sync with a message. Restore it from git or fix it, then rerun. Sync no longer resets it, which made the next run create duplicate issues. - An interrupted run adopts the task sub-issues it already created, so a rerun does not duplicate them. - `done` runs only when you pass it; Project does not move a feature to done by itself. - An organization board needs `ownerType: org`. Init detects it; rerun Init if an older Init recorded `user`. - Project only touches the configured board and issues in the `origin` repository. Package details: [Project README](../../extensions/project/README.md).
